description: GrantFinder AI starter grant database. Curated national and Texas grant opportunities relevant to Catholic parishes and schools. Deadlines and amounts change frequently - always verify on the funder's website before applying.

grants.description: Supports Catholic parishes in under-resourced mission dioceses: church construction and repair, ministry programs, faith formation, and leadership development. Applications typically flow through your diocese.
grants.eligibility_notes: Must be in a Catholic Extension-designated mission diocese; apply through diocesan channels.

grants.description: Funds innovative Catholic projects in evangelization, catechesis, and Catholic culture, including parish and school initiatives.
grants.eligibility_notes: Catholic organizations; project-based proposals.

grants.description: Supports evangelization efforts of the Catholic Church including catechesis, Catholic schools with an evangelizing mission, and religious education.
grants.eligibility_notes: Must be a Catholic organization recognized by the hierarchy; letter of intent process with annual cycle.

grants.grant_name: Raskob Foundation for Catholic Activities Grants
grants.description: Supports Catholic parishes, schools, and organizations across a broad range of needs including education, social services, and capital projects.
grants.eligibility_notes: Must be listed in the Official Catholic Directory or have equivalent Catholic standing.

grants.description: Funds health and wellbeing programs for vulnerable New Yorkers, including programs run by Catholic parishes and schools in New York State.
grants.eligibility_notes: New York State organizations only.

grants.description: Invests in Catholic school vitality and innovation. Much of GHR's grantmaking is by invitation, but their initiatives signal partnership opportunities.
grants.eligibility_notes: Largely invitation-based; strongest presence in Minnesota; monitor for open initiatives.

grants.description: Provides scholarships, operational support, and academic programs for Catholic schools serving Chicago-area communities in need.
grants.eligibility_notes: Chicago area (and affiliated regions) Catholic schools only.

grants.description: Funds projects operated by Catholic women religious (sisters) serving people who are poor and marginalized.
grants.eligibility_notes: Project must be led/administered by Catholic sisters - parishes without women religious leadership are not eligible.

grants.description: Funds women-led ministries and grassroots organizations working for social justice in the Americas, including Catholic parish-based ministries.
grants.eligibility_notes: Women-led initiatives focused on social justice.

grants.description: Federal grants for physical security enhancements at nonprofits at risk of terrorist or hate-motivated attack, including houses of worship and religious schools: cameras, lighting, access control, fencing, training.
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) required; apply through your State Administrative Agency; requires vulnerability assessment; annual cycle typically opens in spring.

grants.description: Small grants from local Walmart stores for community needs including hunger relief, education, and community development. Faith-based organizations are eligible when serving the broader community.
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) or equivalent; program must serve the community regardless of religious affiliation.

grants.description: Funds youth literacy, family literacy, and adult literacy programs. Schools (including private/parochial) and nonprofits within proximity of a Dollar General store are eligible.
grants.eligibility_notes: Must be within a set distance of a Dollar General store; annual application windows.

grants.grant_name: Laura Bush Foundation for America's Libraries
grants.description: Grants to school libraries to expand, update, and diversify book collections. Private and parochial schools are eligible.
grants.eligibility_notes: School libraries serving students; high-need schools prioritized.

grants.grant_name: Toshiba America Foundation K-12 Science/Math Grants
grants.amount: Varies (small grants under ~$5,000 and larger grants)
grants.description: Funds teacher-designed, hands-on classroom projects in science and math for K-12 schools, including private schools.
grants.eligibility_notes: Teacher-led project proposals; rolling deadlines for smaller K-5 grants.

grants.description: Funds youth-led environmental education and stewardship projects at schools and nonprofits, such as school gardens and outdoor learning.
grants.eligibility_notes: Project-based; youth involvement required.

grants.description: Partners with communities to build playgrounds and playspaces for kids. Community organizations, including churches and schools, can apply for build partnerships.
grants.eligibility_notes: Requires community volunteer capacity and demonstrated need for play space.

grants.description: Funds community space projects in small towns (population under 50,000): parks, community centers, and shared spaces. Nonprofits and community groups eligible.
grants.eligibility_notes: Small towns only; quarterly selection cycles.

grants.grant_name: E-Rate Program (Universal Service Schools and Libraries)
grants.description: Federal program providing discounts on internet access and internal network connections for eligible schools, including private and parochial schools, and libraries.
grants.eligibility_notes: Private schools eligible if endowment under $50 million; annual filing windows.

grants.description: Grants and loans for essential community facilities in rural areas (population under 20,000). Nonprofits, including faith-based organizations providing essential community services, may qualify.
grants.contact: Your USDA Rural Development state office
grants.eligibility_notes: Rural areas only; facility must provide an essential service to the community.

grants.funder: The John G. and Marie Stella Kenedy Memorial Foundation
grants.description: Supports Catholic charitable, educational, and religious organizations in Texas, with emphasis on South Texas and the Diocese of Corpus Christi.
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas Catholic organizations; priority to South Texas.

grants.description: Supports Catholic institutions and causes in Texas, including parishes, schools, and Catholic charitable works.
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas Catholic organizations.

grants.description: Challenge grants for capital projects (construction, renovation, major equipment) at nonprofits including religious and educational institutions in Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas, Arkansas, Missouri, and New Mexico.
grants.eligibility_notes: Six-state region (TX, OK, KS, AR, MO, NM); challenge structure requires raising remaining funds.

grants.description: Supports Texas nonprofits across arts, civic, education, health, and human services, including capital and program grants for which faith-affiliated schools and charities may qualify.
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas organizations only.

grants.funder: USCCB Subcommittee on Catholic Home Missions
grants.description: Strengthens the Church in mission dioceses across the United States: evangelization, faith formation, ministry training. Funds flow to dioceses, which support parishes.
grants.eligibility_notes: Apply through your diocese; mission dioceses prioritized.

foundations.notes: Letter of intent process; limits on repeat grants.

foundations.application_cycle: Multiple cycles per year - check website
foundations.focus_areas: Broad Catholic activities: education, social services, capital

foundations.notes: Diocese must be a designated mission diocese.
Funds mostly through large initiatives and intermediary organizations - watch for open initiative rounds.
Monitor for open Catholic school initiatives.

foundations.foundation_name: FADICA (Foundations and Donors Interested in Catholic Activities)
foundations.notes: Not a grantmaker itself, but its member list is a map of Catholic funders to research.
